newsitem.title: UK: LME copper cruises to $2,400 in active pre-market.
newsitem.headline: LME copper cruises to $2,400 in active pre-market.

text.p: Copper probed the psycholgical $2,400 a tonne level in brisk inter-office trade which also saw action in the zinc market.
Copper prices started European trading on the plus side after prices were marked up in Asian hours against the background of a strong yen, traders said.
A drawdown in London Metal Exchange (LME) stocks of 1,750 tonnes -- following last week's net increase of 4,425 tonnes -- was also supportive.
"So far today there's been reasonable two-way business around $2,400 with business coming in from all quarters," a trader said, noting that the April 28 high of $2,407 was capping the rise for now.
"It's quite an important technical level. If it gets above there, copper could go another $40," the trader said.
Three months copper hit a high of $2,405, compared to $2,390 at Friday's kerb close. Cash/threes was little changed at a $58/$63 backwardation.
Aluminium tailed copper higher, aided by a 2,600 stock decline. It was last indicated at $1,677, a gain of $15, and analysts said a move to $1,700 could not be ruled out.
The market was also watching the 1000 GMT March IPAI producer stocks report, which was expected to show more erosion.

"We're seeing a little bit of a bull run in some of the metals. Once it gathers steam, prices will keep going up until they hit some level where producers or big position holders are keen to sell," a trader said.
Zinc prices also nudged higher, probing fresh 4-1/2 year highs, although downward pressure from the Far East was emerging at around $1,340. Prices were at $1,338/40, versus $1,332.
Nickel was slightly firmer at $7,860, up $30, on European-based short covering which traders attributed to follow-through from last week's gains.
The charts showed its next target at $7,900, although a gap between $7,660 and $7,620 might need to be filled, analysts said.
Lead prices edged up to $624/$626, from $622, on the back of firmer zinc.
But technically lead was on shaky territory after Friday's poor close, and and soggy fundamentals would limit the upside, analysts said.
Tin quietly consolidated $10 firmer at $5,880, and was seen sticking to a $5,800-$5,950 range in the near term.
Alloy was indicated marginally higher at $1,510/20.
